description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2022: Advancing FSI Knowledge to Characterize Flexibility Effects in Hurricane-Induced Structural Responses is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Dimitrios Kalliontzis, University of Houston (uh.edu). Fluid-structure interaction (FSI) phenomena involve coupling between the laws of fluid and structural mechanics. Many of these phenomena are encountered in civil infrastructure, including the interaction of coastal structures with fluid motions generated by hurricanes. As the human footprint in coastal regions increases, understanding this interaction becomes more and more critical. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-vmdh-y691. Keywords: fluid-structure interaction, coastal structures, hurricane events, force-based elements, computational fluid dynamics. Published 2023-03-22. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
